newsitem.title: MEXICO: Contal sees sales, profits up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Contal sees sales, profits up in 1996.

text.p: Mexican Coca-Cola bottler Grupo Continental expects sales volume to increase four percent by the end of this year, compared with 1995 and net profits to rise 12 percent, a company official said on Thursday.
"In the remaining months, sales volume could reach a recovery of four percent versus 1995," Contal CFO Miguel Angel Rabago told Reuters.

Contal operates in the central states of Aguascalientes, San Luis Potosi, Zacatecas and Jalisco, areas, he said, where a recovery in purchasing power after last year's economic crisis is beginning to be felt in soft-drink sales.
Rabago said the firm was targetting a rise in net profits of 12 percent at year-end compared with 1995.
He said that profits in the year up to August were up 22 percent, but he expected those to be pared in the closing months of the year by an expected 35 percent increase in the price of sugar cane.
"My objective is to grow 12 percent in real terms in net profits," he said. "We expect a 35 percent increase in the price of sugar cane, a circumstance that will prevent our profits growing more."
In 1995, Contal's sales volumes fell five percent, as Mexico faced a crunching economic crisis and plummeting purchasing power.
